definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry consists of the diagnosis and interpretation of the visual behavior of the human organism by the employment of any means other than surgery. The practice of optometry further consists of the correction of visual anomalies through the prescribing, employment, and use of lenses, prisms, frames, mountings, contact lenses, orthoptic exercises, and visual training, light frequencies, and any other means or methods for the relief, correction, or remedy of any insufficiencies or abnormal conditions of the human visual organism, other than surgery.

drug_authority.value: Certified optometrists may use pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic and treatment purposes; for treatment, may use nonnarcotic oral analgesics, hydrocodone orally (up to 48 hours), Schedule III or IV oral analgesics for ocular pain, and other agents related to eye/adnexa treatment except Schedule I or II controlled substances. May not dispense drugs. May administer by injection (with exceptions) if trained.
drug_authority.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall prohibit the use, administration, or prescription of pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic purposes and treatment of ocular disease in the practice of optometry by optometrists who have received pharmacological training and certification from a properly accredited institution of higher learning and who are certified by the board to use pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic and treatment purposes.
